s: Er schlug sich mit dem Hammer auf den Daumen.
He hit his thumb with the hammer.
sensation, something extraordinary (be it positive or negative)
Die Entlassung des Ministers war ein Hammer.
The minister's dismissal was a sensation.
Der Torwart parierte einen Hammer von der Strafraumgrenze.
The keeper saved a hard shot from the 18-yard line.
Hammer.et:
From Middle High German hamer, from Old High German hamar, from Proto-West Germanic *hamar, from Proto-Germanic *hamaraz, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱmoros, from *h₂éḱmō (“stone”).
Compare Low German Hamer, Dutch hamer, English hammer, West Frisian hammer, D…

s: Hamas (a Palestinian Islamist militant group and political organization)
a topographic or habitational surname with an etymology similar to that of English Hamm
Hamm.et: From Middle Low German ham, hamm (“land enclosed by a river”); cognate with Old English hamm (“enclosure”).

s: Hamm (an independent city in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany)
Hamm.et: From Middle Low German ham, hamm (“land enclosed by a river”); cognate with Old English hamm (“enclosure”).

Hammel.et: From Middle High German hamel, from Old High German hamal (“wether”, also an adjective “castrated”), from Proto-West Germanic *hamal, from Proto-Germanic *hamalaz (“mutilated”). Cognate with Dutch hamel.

s: a semi-formal address form that combines the formal pronoun Sie with the addressee's first name
Sowohl im Privatleben als auch im Beruflichen gibt es jedoch eine vertrackte Alternative, die heute immer mehr in Mode kommt: Das "Hamburger Sie". Es ist die Kombination aus "Sie" mit dem Vornamen.
However, in both private and professional life, there is a tricky alternative that is becoming increasingly popular today: the "Hamburg Sie", a combination of "Sie" with someone's given name.
Hamburger Sie.et: Literally, “Hamburg Sie”, referring to the original location of its usage. See also Hamburger.

s: panicked purchase in order to hoard provisions
A way of voting, functionally comparable to a division in the UK parliament, where the members or delegates leave the hall and re-enter it through three doors marked as aye, nay, and abstention.
Hammelsprung.et: From Hammel (“wether”) + Sprung (“jump”). Thought to be from the idea that (most of) the delegates follow their faction leaders like sheep follow bellwethers.

s: Hamelin (a town, the administrative seat of Hameln-Pyrmont district, Lower Saxony, Germany)
Hameln.et: From Old Saxon *Hamala (“Hamel”), the name of the river on which the town was built. The river’s name is probably a substantivisation of *hamal (“crooked”); compare the English hydronym Hamble. The n in the name of the town is a fossilised dative ending.

s: a surname transferred from the place name
Hameln.et: From Old Saxon *Hamala (“Hamel”), the name of the river on which the town was built. The river’s name is probably a substantivisation of *hamal (“crooked”); compare the English hydronym Hamble. The n in the name of the town is a fossilised dative ending.

s: hamster wheel (circular cage for a small rodent, which rotates vertically as the animal runs at the bottom)
hamster wheel, rat race (situation of hectic, repetitive activity conducted under pressure and with little sense of fulfilment or progress)
Von innen sieht ein Hamsterrad auch aus wie eine Karriereleiter!
From the inside, a hamster wheel also looks like a career ladder!
Solange ich denken kann, habe ich Hämorrhoiden. Viele, viele Jahre habe ich gedacht, ich dürfte das keinem sagen. Weil Hämorrhoiden doch nur bei Opas wachsen. Ich fand die immer sehr unmädchenhaft.
Hämorrhoide.et: From Latin haemorrhoidae, from Ancient Greek αἱμορροίδες (haimorrhoídes), from αἱμόρροος (haimórrhoos, “flowing with blood”), from αἷμα (haîma, “blood”) and the root of ῥέω (rhéō, “flow”).

s: Das Treffen der Kentauren—wird zur Harfe / Von einem Hämling aus Athen gesungen.
The battle with the Centaurs, to be sung / By an Athenian eunuch to the harp.
Hämling.et: From Middle High German hemling, related to Hammel (“wether, castrated ram”).

s: the coat of arms of the German Democratic Republic (East Germany)
Hammer und Zirkel.et: Literally, “hammer and compass”. These symbols represented workers and intelligentsia. (Farmers were represented by the surrounding ears of corn.)

s: a rural district of Lower Saxony; seat: Hamelin
Former spelling of Hammerklavier which is no longer standard.

hämo-.et: From Ancient Greek αἱμο- (haimo-), from αἷμα (haîma, “blood”).

hämato-.et: From Ancient Greek αἵματος (haímatos), genitive singular of αἷμᾰ (haîmă).
